title: Best Composers for Hire (2026): Music for Film, Games and Ads
description: How to hire a composer for film, games, ads or videos: what to include, licensing, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: A composer writes original music that fits your project: a film score, game soundtrack, ad music or background tracks for videos. Custom music gives your work a sound nobody else has and avoids the licensing limits of stock tracks. Projects go wrong when the brief relies on vague adjectives, the music does not fit the timing of the picture, or the license does not cover how you use it. This guide helps you commission music that works.

faq.a: Stock music is faster and cheaper. Custom music fits your project exactly and can be exclusive. Many projects use custom music for key moments and stock for the rest.
It depends on use: online video, ads, games, film festivals, broadcast. Agree on the media, territories, duration and exclusivity in writing.

faq.q: How do I describe the music I want?
faq.a: Reference tracks and time stamps work better than words. Say what you like about each: the instruments, tempo, mood or build.
Usually a mixed WAV, and sometimes stems or loops for games and editing. Ask for the versions you need, such as shorter edits.

faq.q: Does the composer need to see the video?
faq.a: For film, ads and trailers, yes. Music is timed to picture, so send a locked edit if possible.
